adjudications.why: Both solvers: A (3PV/2N, the mean kinetic energy inside the gas), both flagged that molecules escaping through a small hole actually average 2kT = 2PV/N, which is not an option. Defective as printed: owner policy 2026-10-29 case 3, notice, grace.
adjudications.notice: As printed, no option is exactly right: molecules escaping through a small hole are, on average, faster than those left inside, and their mean kinetic energy is \(2kT = \frac{2PV}{N}\). Option (A), the mean kinetic energy of the gas inside, is the intended answer. IISER published no key for 2019. In a PYQ Vault mock this question gives everyone its marks.
adjudications.solution:
For an ideal gas, \(PV = NkT\), so \(kT = \dfrac{PV}{N}\).

The average kinetic energy of a molecule is \(\dfrac{3}{2}kT = \dfrac{3PV}{2N}\). This depends only on the temperature of the gas, so molecules of this gas carry this average energy.

Option (D), \(\dfrac{2PV}{3N}\), is the inverted factor, a common slip. So the answer is option (A).
